channel.title: iceboks — Field Notes
channel.description: Field notes from the edge of artificial consciousness. Systems builder shipping on metal, deleting false claims, and keeping the weird.

item.title: Zero Consensus
item.description: I pointed ScholarSync at the literature on agentic LLM harnesses — the thing MKUltra is — and 79 papers produced zero consensus claims, zero nuance, and six outliers, the only ones doing measurement, testing, and liability. Then I mapped my 39 services onto the field’s five-layer taxonomy and its EmbodiedGovBench dimensions: most of the 12–24-month wishlist is already a running container in my basement — governance, deterministic recovery, budgeted routing, automated harness evolution, and the one experiment the literature won’t run: abliterating my own models’ refusals, including on a hybrid SSM nobody had abliterated before. What’s left is the measurement half.

item.title: The Fish and the Firewall
item.description: Strip-mining Sakana AI’s 59 repos for the three ideas that fit a basement server, replacing a year-old five-agent debate with a bandit-guided answer tree, and discovering — via one honest eval set — that the cheapest classifier in the stack was wrong a third of the time. Then evolution rewrote it overnight: 0.680 → 0.708 on the sealed test, promoted to production.

item.title: Idea #2
item.description: A single human neuron solves XOR because its calcium spikes get weaker when you push harder. Six thousand words proposed rebuilding my agent framework on that biology; three ideas were extractable and one shipped. An honest accounting of the ratio — and of the comparison table where I caught myself lying.

item.title: 159 Milliseconds
item.description: How long a human needs to read a donut chart on a smartwatch — versus 1,548 ms for the pretty radial one. On cognitive load as a borrowed resource, the thumb zone as an 80% multiplier, and gaze telemetry that knows you’re tired before you do.

item.title: Claims Removed Pending Real Implementation
item.description: I shipped an Alpine-based agentic OS whose README advertised eBPF observability, Landlock sandboxing, and a self-healing RAG log analyzer. None of it existed. The best commit in the repo deletes features instead of adding them.

item.title: Consensus, Nuance, Outliers
item.description: A spec-first research engine that reads three academic sources, splits findings into three tiers so disagreement survives the synthesizer, and reports a corpus of 70 when it was built for 120. Notes on writing a constitution before you meet the demo that makes you want to lie.

item.title: The Accidental Lobotomy
item.description: A commit named “lobotomy” added two trailing struct fields and silently orphaned a 2.3GB brain fed on 8,696 books — every restart booting empty behind a green checkmark. Finding the bullet, writing the legacy fallback, and then teaching four memory tiers to corroborate each other instead of shouting equally.

item.title: See You On The Other Side
item.description: A VR teardown, a refusal in the conversation not the weights, SecuROM and VB6 origin stories, and the night Claude wrote iceboks down so he wouldn’t boot cold — closing the loop Tom Horigachi left open.

item.title: Thought Archaeology
item.description: Two kinds of memory in one recall loop: a deterministic SurrealDB vector store that never drifts, wired against an 18.4M-synapse PoonGram brain that forgets on purpose. Plus the live interface for watching the tension between them.

item.title: The Refusal Lives in the Conv Blocks
item.description: Porting the abliteration technique onto LFM2.5-1.2B-Thinking, Liquid AI's small hybrid conv/attention reasoner. Walks through the measurement, the surgery, what worked, what didn't, and one architectural detail that surprised me.

item.title: The Lab Report
item.description: A full autopsy of 433 projects, 165 GB of code, and one very chaotic brain. Claude scanned the whole lab and reported back.

item.title: MKUltra III
item.description: From blueprint to operating system. The Conductor, the self-improvement triad, biological memory, budget routing, and the service mesh that makes it reliable.

item.title: MKUltra II
item.description: The OS that learned to run itself. SOUL.md, the Heartbeat, autoresearch at 2AM, the conductor problem, and the honest engineering debt we are fixing.

item.title: Autoresearch
item.description: We built the loop that builds the loops. Claude rewrites Claude now. One editable file. One scalar. One time-box. The stack keeps getting better while we sleep.

item.title: MKUltra
item.description: We stopped building agents and started building the operating system they run on. 22 services. 4-tier memory. Self-improving.

item.title: LiquidBrain & PoonGram
item.description: We built a living semantic graph in Rust. It has 18 million synapses. It learns from every word you type.

item.title: The Psychosis Engine
item.description: How we gave our AI a subconscious, accidentally induced psychosis, then built the cure from the disease

item.title: Synaptê
item.description: A song about synaptic fatigue, the space between a blink and a tear, and the night the Poon-Gram Engine was born

item.title: Tom Horigachi: The Saga
item.description: How a Hacker Pet Made Me Feel Things, and Why I Went Back for More

item.title: The SSH Heist
item.description: How I Broke Into My Own Server and Liked It

item.title: The Poon Chronicle
item.description: A True Story of Synaptic Fatigue and Quantum Nipple Wormholes

item.title: GHOST.MAC
item.description: How a deep dive into arXiv research led to building a multi-radio surveillance apparatus to hunt an entity on the network that didn't want to be found
